name: Kelvex Transit Ground Crew Night Shift Rig
description: A head-to-toe kit built for Kelvex MagRail ground crews pulling overnight platform maintenance shifts. The jacket is a structured navy synth-canvas shell with a broad safety-orange chevron running diagonally across the chest and back, retro-reflective tape stitched along the cuffs and collar seam, and the Kelvex wordmark embroidered in silver thread above the left breast pocket. Underneath sits a charcoal thermal base layer with a mock-neck collar that folds up against wind off the rail corridors. The trousers are Kelvex-branded heavy-duty stretch twill in navy, with reinforced knee panels, a wide tool loop on the right thigh, and a magnetic-closure cargo pocket that holds standard-issue platform tablets. Boots are a steel-toe mid-height lace-up in matte black with orange contrast stitching and a slip-resistant rubber outsole rated for wet platform grating. A Kelvex-issue hard shell helmet in hi-vis yellow clips to a carabiner loop on the jacket's left hip when not worn. Gloves tuck into the back waistband — insulated synth-leather palms, knit back panels.
functionality: Retro-reflective panels for rail-corridor visibility, reinforced knees for platform crawlwork, magnetic cargo pocket for transit tablets, tool loop for handheld diagnostics, thermal base layer for unheated maintenance tunnels, helmet carabiner loop, insulated grip gloves
what_it_says: This is someone who keeps M88 moving whether anyone sees them or not. The Kelvex branding marks them as company property on shift — reliable, unglamorous, essential. The orange chevron signals hazard proximity without apology. Off-shift, the jacket stays on because it's warm and it's theirs.
manufacturer: Kelvex Transit Systems — issued uniform, supplemented with Ironpass thermal base layer
price_range: Φ180–Φ240 (company-issued; replacement cost out of pocket)
story_hooks: A ground crew worker discovers a structural fault in the rail during a night shift that their supervisor ordered them to log as routine — the Kelvex jacket's embedded shift-ID makes them traceable if they report it officially.
The retro-reflective chevron catches a security camera's light at the wrong moment, placing a worker at a platform where a body was found between the 02:00 and 04:00 maintenance windows.
A veteran crew member's jacket has a small hand-stitched patch over the Kelvex logo — a quiet act of defiance that's gotten others quietly fired.
